answer: You address a recipient, which is an identity. The name can contain dots, so `@pete.smith` and `@sam.rivera` each count as one mention. You don't have to declare it first. Mentioning `@sales` is enough to make `sales` a known identity (see `At-Mention.md` and `Recipient.md`).

10	A **recipient** is an [[Identity]] you address. When mentioned with `@name`, it is indexed to be queried, and clicking it in the editor will open the “Mentions Inbox”.
11	
12	See [[At-Mention]] for the `@name` syntax, and [[Identity]] for where names come from (accounts, `identity.define`, or simply being mentioned).
13	
14	# The Mention Inbox
15	The Mention Inbox is a [[View|view]] listing open `@mention`s, grouped by page. It opens in the right sidebar by default, and its dock menu can move it to the left sidebar, bottom panel, or a modal. Open it with `Navigate: Mentions`, or by clicking any mention.
16	
17	# The `recipients` attribute
18	Every mention also sets a `recipients` attribute onto the object that hosts it, holding the `@name` identifier of each name mentioned.
19	* a mention inside a task or list item stamps that task or item.
20	* a mention in a plain paragraph or header stamps the **page** object instead.
21	
22	Pages can also declare recipients declaratively in frontmatter — useful when a whole page is “for” someone without inline mentions:
23	
24	```yaml
25	---
26	recipients: ["pete", "sales"]
27	---
28	```
29	
30	Like `tags`, the value can also be written as a plain string, cut on whitespace:
31	
32	```yaml
33	---
34	recipients: pete sales
35	---
36	```
37	
38	# Addressing vs. crediting
39	A mention only ever means one thing: *this is for you*. Marking text as *written by* someone instead uses a slightly different syntax, see [[Authorship]].
40	
41	# Querying mentions
42	At-mentions are indexed like any other [[Object Index|relation]], with `kind == "at-mention"`. `to` is always the `@name` identifier (`toTag == "identity"`) and `alias` holds the name as typed. Build your own view over them with SLIQ, for example @sam.rivera:
43	
44	${query[[
45	  from index.relations "at-mention"
46	  where _.to == "@sam.rivera"
47	  select { page = _.page, snippet = _.snippet }
48	]]}
49	
50	Frontmatter declarations are relations too, with `kind == "recipients"`.
51	
52	For a complete request, reply and resolution workflow, see [[Guide/Comments, Mentions and Replies]].

9:An **at-mention** is the `@name` span you type in text. It refers to an [[Identity]], and it has two directions: written plainly it *addresses* that identity, making it a [[Recipient]], or when used as a signature it *credits* that identity instead, see [[Authorship]].
12:Type `@` followed by a name with no spaces, e.g. @jo. While typing, autocomplete offers every known identity.
14:A name may contain dots, so dotted usernames carry whole: @pete.smith and @sam.rivera are each one mention.
16:**Any name is a valid mention.** Nothing needs declaring up front: mentioning @sales makes `sales` a known identity. See [[Identity]] for more info.
